history.summary: One of the 51 (some counts say 52/108) Shakti Peethas: legend holds that Sati's navel (nabhi) fell here as Shiva carried her body. Perched atop Annapurna peak at ~910 m (3,000 ft). Also called Punyagiri, for the Kali river is said to descend here and become the Sharda in the plains. A local legend tells of a merchant's copper temple (the 'Jhuthe ka Mandir' of Tanakpur) that could not be moved forward after he broke a vow of a gold shrine. Famous for mundan (first hair-cutting) ceremonies of children. A 2-3 month Purnagiri Mela is held during Chaitra Navratri drawing lakhs of pilgrims. TOWN CORRECTION: CSV lists town as 'Udham Singh Nagar' (a district name, not a town) and state as Uttarakhand; corrected to Tanakpur, Champawat district. Geocoded coordinates are for the Tanakpur/Poornagiri area; the hilltop shrine itself lies ~20 km away on the peak - coordinates approximate (verify).

name: Purnagiri Temple
town_description: Tanakpur is a small town in Champawat district of Uttarakhand's Kumaon region, on the banks of the Sharda river near the Nepal border. It is the railhead of the region with trains to Delhi and Lucknow, and serves as the base town for the Purnagiri pilgrimage.

travel.road: Motorable road from Tanakpur to Thuligad; then a 3 km paved trek (stone steps) to the shrine. Tanakpur has bus and shared-taxi links to Haldwani, Nainital, Bareilly and Delhi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to May; Chaitra Navratri (March-April) for the Purnagiri Mela (extremely crowded). Avoid the monsoon (July-August) when trek paths are slippery.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open year-round. During Navratri the temple often stays open round the clock; at other times night closures are announced by the temple committee (verify).
